name: Emergency, standby and UPS power systems
principle: A facility secures loads that must not fail through layers: battery-backed uninterruptible power supplies (classified VFI, VI or DXI by output dependency under IEC 62040-3) ride through the first seconds, standby generating sets start and close onto the emergency bus, and automatic transfer switching restores normal supply after the outage. Emergency generation is sized for essential process, fire and life-safety loads; batteries carry instrumentation, control and safety systems through the transition and support black-start of larger units.

process_steps.name: UPS carries critical loads from batteries
Standby genset starts and closes onto the emergency bus
Load shed/blocks restored in priority sequence
Normal supply returns; retransfer and battery recharge

performance.basis: standby generators and UPS output at the TNB LV level

performance.metric: required periodic inspection for MV installations
performance.basis: Energy Commission inspection frequency above 11 kV to 132 kV

limitations: batteries age invisibly without a tested maintenance and capacity programme
gensets need periodic load-bank runs to avoid wet stacking and prove start reliability
advantages: layered ride-through keeps safety instrumented and control systems alive
black-start-capable units let facilities recover without grid support

sources.note: IEC 62040 UPS series, IEC web catalogue
HSE guidance on electrical safety and duty of care for emergency systems, read 2026-11-07
TNB voltage and fault-level tables, read 2026-11-13
